subject: Private VPC architecture scrub — control/data split and operational runbook
messages:
From: Matthew Stokes <matthew.stokes@acme.example>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: acme-networking@acme.example
Date: 2026-08-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Private VPC architecture scrub before pilot

Michael —

Thanks for taking this on. Acme is finalizing the on-prem pilot procurement and our NetOps lead asked for a short architecture scrub focused on the control plane / data plane separation and a clear operational picture for day-0 -> day-30. Key asks from our side:

- Confirm control plane endpoints that must be reachable from our management network (ports + expected FQDNs).
- Data plane egress constraints (we need to demonstrate no unexpected egress to third-party cloud control planes).
- A runbook snippet for a canary rollout (how we fall back to hosted Redwood and how KV cache warming is handled).
- Evidence of KMS integration paths and who holds keys.

Can we get a short readout and a diagram by EOD Thursday (2026-08-06)? We have a tight procurement window.

Thanks —
Matt Stokes
NetOps Manager, Acme Corp.
attachments: none

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Matthew Stokes <matthew.stokes@acme.example>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC architecture scrub before pilot

Matt —

Appreciate the clear list. We're on it. High-level plan:

1) Today: quick readout email answering your three network bullets + a reference diagram.
2) Tomorrow morning: 30-minute call to walk the diagram and runbook snippet; capture any action items.
3) Thursday EOD: deliver a concise ops-runbook PDF and the canary matrix.

Quick answers (detail to follow in the diagram we attached):
- Control plane endpoints: we list two FQDNs (control.redwood-inference.net and control-ops.redwood-inference.net) on TCP/443 and TCP/8443 for mutual TLS. We can provide IP ranges for allowlisting but recommend FQDN plus TLS cert pinning when possible.
- Data plane egress: runtime nodes only egress to customer-provided artifact registries and our collector endpoints over TLS; no controlplane metadata is streamed to public clouds. We will provide a minimal egress ACL example.
- Canary: we suggest a 3-stage canary (5%, 30%, 100%) with KV cache seeding during the 30% stage. See attached matrix.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS supported via our KMS proxy; keys never leave customer KMS (we only receive wrapped keys).

I've attached an annotated reference diagram (redwood-private-vpc-refdiagram-v2.png) and a starter canary matrix (canary-deploy-matrix.xlsx). Please confirm a 9:00am PT slot tomorrow for the walk-through.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Director, Deployments — Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-private-vpc-refdiagram-v2.png (image/png), canary-deploy-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matthew Stokes <matthew.stokes@acme.example>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-05T13:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC architecture scrub before pilot

Michael / Matt —

Quick technical clarifications to the readout:

> - Control plane endpoints: we list two FQDNs (...) on TCP/443 and TCP/8443 for mutual TLS.

We should call out one more detail: the control plane also listens on an internal-only port (TCP/9000) when deployed in "private" mode for bootstrap operations; that port must be reachable from the customer's management VLAN during provisioning window and may be closed afterwards if the customer prefers.

> - Data plane egress: runtime nodes only egress to customer-provided artifact registries and our collector endpoints over TLS; no controlplane metadata is streamed to public clouds.

Addendum: observability data (traces/metrics) are pushed to the collector endpoint; customers can choose to host the collector on-prem (recommended) or endpoint to a dedicated VPC in their cloud account. If they host on-prem, the egress footprint is zero.

Action items for the call:
- Confirm whether Acme wants collector on-prem or to point at a dedicated Acme cloud VPC.
- Decide on allowlist strategy: FQDN pinning vs IP ranges.
- Confirm KMS provider (AWS KMS vs on-prem HSM) so Jonas can prepare the evidence artifact.

I also added a short troubleshooting checklist to the diagram notes (see attached).

— Irene
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments referenced in diagram notes: kms-access-evidence.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matthew Stokes <matthew.stokes@acme.example>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-06T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC architecture scrub before pilot

Team / Matt —

Summary from today's 9:00am PT call and commitments:

Decisions made:
- Collector will be on-prem (zero egress) per Acme preference.
- Allowlist strategy: Acme will allowlist our control FQDNs + open TCP/9000 for provisioning window. Fallback = Cert pinning.
- KMS: Acme chooses on-prem HSM. Redwood will integrate via KMS proxy; keys remain in HSM.

Deliverables (owners / ETA):
- Updated reference diagram with controlplane bootstrap note and observability placement — Michael (ETA 2026-08-06 EOD).
- Canary matrix finalized with KV-warm sequence and rollback steps — Michael/Jonas (ETA 2026-08-06 EOD).
- KMS evidence artifact and HSM integration checklist — Jonas (ETA 2026-08-07 11:00am PT).
- Runbook snippet for cutover rollback and hotspot mitigation — Irene (ETA 2026-08-06 EOD).

Attachments pushed to the shared Drive folder and JIRA ticket INF-2147 for traceability.

Notes for procurement: the updated runbook will include a minimal SLA exception clause for the provisioning window and a simple checklist the Acme SOC can sign off on — Naomi will coordinate the procurement evidence.

— Jonas Weber
Principal Architect, Redwood Inference
attachments: none (refer to Drive)

From: Matthew Stokes <matthew.stokes@acme.example>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-07T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Private VPC architecture scrub before pilot

Jonas / Michael —

Thanks for the walk-through and the rapid follow-ups. The diagram looks good and the canary matrix answers our key questions. We confirm: on-prem collector + on-prem HSM.

Next steps for us: procurement will ask for the runbook PDF and the KMS checklist to attach to the PO by EOD Monday. Can you get the KMS checklist and the signed runbook snippet into INF-2147? If you can, I can route the PO and we should be green.

Appreciate the responsiveness —
Matt
NetOps Manager, Acme Corp.
attachments: none
